newsitem.title: TURKEY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FACTS AND FIGURES FOR FENERBAHCE-GALATASARAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FACTS AND FIGURES FOR FENERBAHCE-GALATASARAY.

text.p: Facts and figures for Sunday's showcase Turkish first division match between Fenerbahce and Galatasaray at the Fenerbahce stadium.
Fenerbahce: Founded in 1907. They have won the Turkish league a record 13 times.
Best performance in Europe: European Cup Winners' Cup quarter-finals 1964.
Ground: Fenerbahce Stadium, capacity, 28,000.
Trainer: Sebastiao Lazaroni.
Record league appearances: Mucdat Yetkiner, 760.
Record league victory: 9-1 v Samsunspor in 1993-94 season
Galatasaray: Founded in 1905 as Galatasaray Physical Education Club by a group of students at Istanbul's Galatasaray Lycee. They are Turkey's second-oldest club after Besiktas (1903).
Best performance in Europe: European Cup semifinals 1989.
Ground: Ali Sami Yen Stadium, capacity, 33,000.
Trainer: Fatih Terim.
Record number of goals: Metin Oktay, 608 league and cup goals.
Record league victory: 9-2 v Adanademispor in 1983-84 season Fascinating facts:
- After drawing in the final of the Prime Minister's Cup in 1958, Fenerbahce and Galatasaray decided to share the cup and cut it down the middle.
- Galatasaray Sports Club possess a wealth of sports facilities including their own island in the Bosphorus straits equipped with its own swimming pool, boathouse, restaurant, discotheque and casino.

- Fatih Terim is only the ninth Turk to coach Galatasaray out of 42 trainers in the club's history. These have included 12 Englishmen, three Germans and two Scots; Billy Hunter who managed the club from 1924-1927 and Graeme Souness, who despite taking Galatasaray to cup victory, was replaced by Terim at the beginning of this season.
- Galatasaray's red and yellow strip was first worn by the team on December 6, 1908 in a match against a team from the British vessel H.M.S. Barham anchored off Istanbul at the time.
- Galatasaray are known to their fans as "Jim Bom Bom" from a song imported from Switzerland and adopted by Galatasaray fans.

- A match between the two sides on February 23, 1934 was abandoned after a fight broke out between the players which resulted in various punishments being meted out to 17 of them, including the Fenerbahce goalkeeper who was banned for life.
- Galatasaray were the first Turkish team to play abroad, when they travelled to play Hungarian team, Closvar after domestic fixtures were interrupted by the Balkan War of 1911-1912.
- The first match played at Galatasaray's Ali Sami Yen stadium between Turkey and Bulgaria on December 20, 1964, was marred by a fire in which one person was killed and 84 injured.
- Of the 76 Turkish league games played between Fenerbahce and Galatasaray, Fenerbahce have won 26, Galatasaray 23 and 27 matches have ended in a draw.

- Fenerbahce and Galatasaray have met a total of 326 times in their history, Fenerbahce have won 121 times and Galatasaray 104 times, 101 matches have ended in a draw. Fenerbahce have scored 451 goals against Galatasaray's 411.
- Fenerbahce and Galatasary are two of only four teams to have won the Turkish league title. The others are Besiktas (nine) and Trabzonspor (six).
- Fenerbahce were the first Turkish club to have a site on the internet.
- Fenerbahce were the first team to beat Manchester United at Old Trafford in 40 years of European competition when they recorded a 1-0 win in October in the European Champions' League.

- Fenerbahce chairman Ali Sen, currently banned from the directors' box for insulting a referee, this week fined midfielder Kemalettin Sentuk 500 million Turkish Lira ($4,300) after he was sent off on Sunday for swearing. "Such an action does not befit a Fenerbahce member," said Sen.
